name: P01 a paragraph of two lines has no line to scan (the count guard raised)
P02 a count of 1 is a paragraph the scan starts again for (the guard lowered to < 1, which for a whole count is also <= 0)
P04 the paragraph's start is not floored at the first line
P05 a different list of lines is not a new paragraph
P06 a different start is not a new paragraph
P07 a list that has become shorter is not a new paragraph
why: computeRegions never shortens bodyLines; the read-count row of the oracle kills it.

name: P08 the first line of the paragraph is read too
P09 the second line of the paragraph is not read
P10 a new paragraph keeps the indents of the old one
P11 every second line is read
P12 the lines that do NOT match the list are the ones kept
P13 every kept indent is 0 (always an interrupter)
P14 every kept indent is one column too deep
P15 every kept indent is one column too shallow
P16 the code-depth test is inverted
P17 the open columns are ignored
P18 a kept indent that is not code answers no
P19 no kept indent is looked at
P20 the lines are kept as a copy, so the key never matches (a clock mutant: every answer is right)
why: Every answer is right and every question reads the paragraph again: killed by the clock rows of pathological-inputs.test.ts (an interrupter far down a paragraph), and by the oracle's 200,000-question rows, which stop at their time budget.

name: Q01 every line that is not code interrupts the paragraph
G01 the scan is asked for every line (the gate removed)
why: Killed by the 'how often the scan is asked' rows of paragraph-interrupt-wiring.test.ts and by the clock pin of two lines that alternate the open columns (without the gate the scan is asked for every line; the memo no longer depends on the columns, so it is also cheap, but the count rows hold the contract).

name: G02 the scan is asked only for a level 1 underline
G03 the scan is asked only for a level 2 underline
G04 an uninterrupted paragraph loses its title
G05 an interrupted paragraph keeps its whole title
G06 a line that cannot underline holds the whole paragraph as its count (the review round's regression: every answer is right, a long first line is measured again by every later line)
why: A clock mutant: killed by the rows with a first line of 20,000 quote markers in pathological-inputs.test.ts.

name: G07 the answer of the scan is taken the wrong way round
G08 a line that cannot underline holds 0 lines as its count (the default reader's one-line title is lost)
why: Not equivalent, although it reads so: the default count is 1 for the line below a single paragraph line, and the default reader (and from: markdown) underlines exactly that one line, so a title of 0 lines loses its heading. Killed by the wiring row that reads a one-line title under the default reader.

name: G09 the scan reads the CommonMark entries' columns only
why: Found by Session 332's first mutation run: no row told `columns()` from `commonmarkColumns()` until the wiring rows for an indented bullet followed by a letter-marker item (a pandoc-only container column that makes the bullet an interrupter) were added.

name: G10 the scan is told the run length and not the title length
why: Equivalent: `wholeParagraph` is `consecutiveBody` under a CommonMark reader unless the run opens a non-paragraph, and then it is `defaultTitleLineCount`, which both spellings return.

name: G11 a new scan for every question (a clock mutant: every answer is right)
G12 the four columns of an underline start at the column 0
G13 the four columns of an underline run the other way
G14 the underline of a CommonMark reader is asked of the other readers
G15 setextLevel takes a level 1 whatever the underline
G16 the scan is handed the paragraph one line longer than it is
why: Found by the review round's mutation lens: a paragraph that starts below the first line of the document, with an interrupter as its first line, tells it apart; every earlier row started its paragraph at body index 0, where the floor hides the extra line.
